events.title: Work begins on the Suez Canal
events.description: Engineers broke ground at the Mediterranean end of what would become the Suez Canal in Egypt. The project went on for ten years.
events.significance: The canal opened in 1869. It created a direct shipping route between Europe and Asia and changed global trade and naval strategy.

events.title: Allied forces land at Gallipoli
events.description: Australian, New Zealand, British, French and Indian troops came ashore on the Gallipoli Peninsula in the Ottoman Empire. They hoped to open a sea route to Russia and knock the Ottomans out of World War I.
events.significance: The campaign ended in an Allied withdrawal. It left a deep mark on national identity in Australia and New Zealand, which mark April 25 each year as ANZAC Day.

events.title: Watson and Crick publish the structure of DNA
events.description: James Watson and Francis Crick published their paper in the journal Nature. It described DNA as a double helix, building on X-ray work by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.
events.significance: The discovery explained how genetic information is stored and copied. It laid the foundations of modern molecular biology and genetics.

events.title: The Carnation Revolution begins in Portugal
events.description: Military officers launched a coup that overthrew the authoritarian Estado Novo regime. Civilians poured into the streets and put carnations in soldiers' rifles, and almost no blood was shed.
events.significance: The revolution ended decades of dictatorship and led to democracy in Portugal. It also led to the independence of Portugal's African colonies.
